parakeet: If a community can be conditioned to believe a medieval hoax as the burial cloth of Christ, what else can they be led to believe? Many Christians claim to follow a tradition grounded in historical truth. Jesus really lived, really died, really resurrected. But when something like the shroud is embraced, despite evidence of inauthenticity, the criteria for truth quietly shifts from is this objectively real to does this inspire devotion? That shift de-anchors faith from evidence. It paves the way for pseudo-archaeology, which we see in Noah's Ark being discovered every decade, fabricated artifacts like fake nails from the crucifixion, and then even false claims of miracles. Once meaning outranks fact, anything becomes sacred. If a community can be conditioned to believe a medieval hoax is the burial cloth of Christ, what else can they be led to believe? This opens the door to manipulative religious leaders, political propaganda disguised as divine will, anti intellectualism and education and science, faith untethered from evidence becomes compliance disguised as conviction.
